sentences.text: 1 This petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989 is filed seeking compensation for the death of Chandramma W/o. A.R.Satish in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated in the petition that on 12-08-2023 at about 9.00 p.m., while deceased was getting down from the BMTC bus bearing No.KA-57-FA-3114 (herein after called as offending vehicle) at Medahalli bus stop, on Old Madras road, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of the offending bus suddenly moved the bus without observing deceased in a rash and negligent manner.

As a result,
deceased fell down from the bus and sustained multiple injuries
Immediately, she was taken to Government Hospital, K.R. puram, thereafter she shifted to Victoria hospital as impatient for a period of one month.
She has not recovered from accidental injuries and died on 13-09- 2023 during treatment.

After the postmortem dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed the last rites of the deceased by spending Rs.1,00,000/-.
3.
It is stated that the accident and death was due to negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
At the time of accident, the deceased was aged about 37 years, working as a flower vendor and was earning .30,000/- p.m.

The Petitioner No.1 is the husband and Petitioner No.2 is the daughter of deceased and they were depending upon the income of deceased and due to untimely death of Chandramma, they have suffered mental shock and agony and lost their bread earner of the family.
Therefore, it is requested to award .50,00,000/- compensation with interest from the Respondent.
4. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent has appeared before the court through his counsel and filed the written statement.
5. The Respondent has appeared before the court and filed the objections denying negligence of its driver.

It has contended that the offending bus was proceeding from Hosakote bu stop to Kempegowda bus stop and the bus reached Medahalli bus stop, after alighting passenger, the driver was moving slowly and at the same time, the door closing slowly, by that time, the deceased Chandramma ran getting down from the moving bus hurriedly and negligently, the door dashed and she lost control, fallen from the bus, which resulted in accident and death and the alleged accident occurred due to negligence of deceased only.
It has denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and contended that compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that the death of Chandramma W/o.
A.R.Satish was only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of BMTC bus bearing No.KA-57-FA- 3114 on 12-08-2023 about 9-00 p.m., near Medahalli bus stop, OM Road, Medahalli, Bengaluru District ?

7. In support of their claim, 1 st Petitioner is examined as PW.1 and MRT at Victoria hospital is examined as Pw-2 and got marked a documents at Ex.P.1 to 22.
8. The Respondent has examined the Gynecologist at K.R.Puram Govt. hospital as RW-1 and got marked the copy of MLC at Ex.R.1.
Further the driver of offending bus is examined as RW.2 and no documents are got marked.
9. I heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

10. By considering the evidence and materials available on record and after hearing the arguments my findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3:

As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 11. ISSUE NO.1:- In order to prove their claim, Petitioners relied on the police and medical records.
PW-1 husband of the deceased has deposed that on 12-08-2023 at 9.00 p.m., while deceased was getting down from the offending bus at Medahalli bus stop, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of the offending bus suddenly moved the bus without observing deceased in a rash and negligent manner.

As a result, deceased fell down from the bus and sustained multiple injuries Immediately, she was taken to Government Hospital, K.R. puram, thereafter she shifted to Victoria hospital as impatient for a period of one month.
She has not recovered from accidental injuries and died on 13-09- 2023 during treatment.
It is stated that the accident was solely due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending bus.
12. The learned counsel for the plaintiff vehemently argued that The evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.

Occurrence of accident due to rash and negligent driving of the bus driver and relied upon the decisions rendered in AI R 2019 SC 994 between Sunita and Ors V Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation and Anr and ILR 2016 KAR 55 between M/s ICICI Lombard GIC Ltd Vs Smt Bharthi Reddy and others.

sentences.text: 13. keeping in view of contentions raised by the parties and above said decisions, I have perused the material available on record.

To substantiate the case, Petitioners have produced copy of FIR at Ex.P1, FIS at Ex.P2, police requisition and police notice at EX P3 and 4. Pm report spot at EX P4,
FSL report at EX P6 inquest at EX P7 spot Mahazar and rough sketch at Ex.P.8 and EXP9, IMV report at Ex.P.10, charge sheet at Ex.P.11.
On perusal of FSL, it appears that death is due to injury sustained to the left lower limb.

3 14.
Petitioners say that the injuries sustained by the deceased were not healed and due to the accidental injuries she died during the course of treatment.
15. The Respondent denied negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.
He says that it was the negligence of the Petitioner in causing the accident.
There is no nexus between the accidental injuries and death.
It is stated that there was no negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
Driver of the Respondent was examined as RW1 and reiterated the contention of the written statement.
16. It was suggested to PW-1 that the deceased was died due to other reasons and not due to accidental injuries.
It is contended that there are no documents to show that the deceased was under continues treatment and died of the accidental injuries.
PW-1 has denied all the suggestions and stated that the death of his wife was due to accidental injuries only.
17. Due to accidental injuries, she was treated for the accidental injuries in victoria hospital and admitted as impatient for a period of one month .
FSL report shows that Chandramma died due to accidental injuries.

By considering all these facts and circumstances, medical records available on record, it is held that Chandramma had sustained grievous injury in the alleged accident and she was in the Victoria hospital from date of the accident till her death, she was taking continuous treatment and died of this accidental injuries only.
18. There are no materials on record to disprove the Petitioners' evidence and to prove the contention of the Respondent.
The evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
After the investigation, police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and the copy of the charge sheet is produced at Ex.P.11.
Charge sheet prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
From all the above materials clearly indicate that the accident was due to the negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
Based on the entire records, I hold that the driver of offending vehicle was negligent in causing the accident due to which Chandramma died due to injuries sustained in the RTA.
19. Issue No.2:
Petitioners states that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Chandramma.
The Petitioner No.1 is the husband and Petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased.
They have produced the Aadhaar card of Petitioners and deceased at Ex.P.14 to 16, which clearly indicates that deceased is the wife of Petitioner No.1 and the mother of Petitioner No.2.
Hence, I hold that the Petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased and they are entitled for compensation as dependents.
20. It is stated that the deceased was 37 years old and was working as a flower vendor and was earning .30,000/- p.m. and was the sole earning member of the family.
In order to show the avocation and income of the deceased Petitioners have not produced any supportive documents.

sentences.text: the absence of proof of income, by considering age of the deceased and date of accident, notional income of Rs.16,000/- per month is taken.
21. According to the Ex-P-16 - Aadhaar card, the year of birth of deceased is mentioned as 1986.
As per this document her age was 37 years as on the date of accident and same is considered as age of the deceased and proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 15.
As the age of the deceased is between 30-40 years, 40% future prospects is to be added as per Pranay Sethi case.
Then the monthly income would be .22,400/-.

As there are 2 dependents, as per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 1/3rd of the income to be deducted towards her personal and living expenses and then the annual income would come around .14,934 x 12 = .1,79,208/- and by applying 15 multiplier, the loss of dependency would be .26,88,120/-.
22. CONSORTIUM:

sentences.text: 23. Loss to estate:
It appears that the Petitioner No.1 has lost his wife at his younger age and daughter has lost her mother.
Hence, .20,000/- is awarded towards loss to estate.
1 24. Funeral Expenses:
Petitioners have claimed that they have spent .1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral & obsequies ceremony expenses.
By considering the facts and circumstances it would be proper to award .15,000/- for the funeral and other incidental expenses.
25. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioners have relied on 18 medical bills for .17,978/- at Ex.P.19.
Though counsel for Respondent has cross-examined the PW-1, nothing has been elicited to disprove the medical bills.
The medical bills appears to be genuine.

Hence, Petitioner is awarded .17,978/-
towards Medical Expenses.
26. In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the Petitioner under various headings is as follows :

27. Liability:
The Petitioners have lead cogent evidence and have proved that the accident was occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle.
Hence, Respondent being the owner of the offending bus is liable to pay the above compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. to the Petitioners.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
28. ISSUE NO.3 :
In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioners are awarded compensation of .28,21,098/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the realization.
Respondent shall deposit the compensation amount within three months from the date of this order.
After deposit of amount, 10% of the amount is apportioned to 1st Petitioner and 90% to the Petitioner No.2.

Out of the said apportioned amount in respect of Petitioner No.2, 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in her name in any nationalized or scheduled bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and balance 75% amount shall be disbursed to her through E-payment on proper identification.
The entire apportioned amount in respect of Petitioner No.1 shall be disbursed to him through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, corrected, signed and pronounced by me in open court dated this the 6th day of February 2025).
